parts.title: The story
parts.say: Tell me how this started. What made you want to build this?

q.q: How did the idea start?
q.hint: Let them talk. Capture the words they use; those words go into the spec.

q.q: If you described the app in one sentence to a friend, what would you say?
What problem does it solve, and for whom?
How do those people handle this today, without the app?
q.hint: WhatsApp groups, spreadsheets, phone calls, a competitor. The current workaround sets the bar the app has to beat.

q.q: Why now? Is something pushing the timing?

parts.title: Who uses it
parts.say: Let me make sure I understand everyone who would touch this.

q.q: Who are the different kinds of people who would use it?
q.hint: Customers, drivers, shop owners, admins. Each type usually means its own login and its own screens.

q.q: At launch, roughly how many people would use it?
Who runs it behind the scenes? What do they need to see or change?
Do people need accounts? How should they sign in?
q.hint: Phone number, email, Google or Apple, invite only.

parts.title: What it must do
parts.say: Now the part I care about most. I want to find the smallest version that is still worth launching.

q.q: If the app could only do ONE thing on day one, what would it be?
q.hint: This is the first version. Everything else is version two.

q.q: What are the three to five things it absolutely must do?
Walk me through it. A person opens the app for the first time. What happens, step by step, until they are done?
Is there an app that is close to what you imagine? What would you keep, and what would you change?
q.hint: The single most useful scoping question. Get the actual app names.

q.q: What would be nice to have later, but could wait?
Is there anything you have decided it should NOT do?

parts.title: Where it runs
parts.say: A few practical ones about where and how people will use it.

q.q: Where does it need to run?
Which languages should it support?
q.hint: Persian and Arabic mean right-to-left layout, planned from day one.

q.q: Which countries or cities will it be used in?
q.hint: Affects payments, SMS, app store accounts and privacy law.

q.q: Does it need to work without internet?

parts.title: Connections and money
parts.say: Does anything outside the app need to be involved? Payments, maps, messages, other systems?

q.q: Does money move through the app? Who pays whom, and how?
q.hint: One-time, subscription, per order, or cash outside the app. An app that holds money between two parties is a different size of project.

q.q: What should it connect to?
Do you already use software this would need to talk to?
Who creates the content in the app (listings, posts, products)? You, or the users?

parts.title: Data and trust
parts.say: What kind of information will the app be holding about people?

q.q: What kinds of information will it hold?
Any requirement about where the data is stored?
o: Must stay in another specific country

q.q: Any rules or regulations you know apply to this kind of business?
q.hint: In Ontario: PIPEDA for personal data, PHIPA if health data is involved. Note it, do not advise.

parts.title: What exists already
parts.say: What do you already have in hand that I could look at?

q.q: Does it have a name? A domain? A logo?
What exists today?
o: A spreadsheet or database of data

q.q: Have you worked with developers or an agency on this before? What happened?
q.hint: A previous build that stalled is context, not a red flag on its own. Ask what they have from it.

q.q: What can you send me after the call?

parts.title: The business
parts.say: How does this work as a business, or what is it for?

q.q: How will it make money, or what is it for?
o: Free, it supports an existing business
Internal tool for our own company

q.q: Who is the paying customer, and is that the same person as the user?
Have you talked with people who would use it? What did they say?
Six months after launch, what would make you say it worked?

parts.title: Timeline and budget
parts.say: Two questions people sometimes find awkward. I ask them plainly because they decide what we can propose.

q.q: Is there a date this needs to be ready by? What is driving it?
Do you have a budget range in mind for the first version?
q.hint: Ask it straight and do not react to the number. "No idea" is a fine answer; it means you propose options.

q.q: Would you be open to launching a smaller first version and growing it?
o: No, it needs to be complete

q.q: After launch, who looks after it?
o: We would want you to maintain it

parts.title: Working together
parts.say: Last few, about how we would work if we go ahead.

q.q: Who makes the final decisions on this project?
Who would I talk to day to day, and how do you prefer to communicate?
How often would you want to see progress?
Do you expect to own the code and the accounts at the end?
o: Happy for the developer to host it
q.hint: Recommend yes. It protects them and it protects you.

q.q: Are you talking with other developers as well?
q.hint: Either answer is fine. It tells you how to position the proposal.

q.q: What questions do you have for me?

parts.title: Wrap-up
parts.say: Here is what happens next: I will write up what I heard, go through it with my team, and come back within a few days with questions, a suggested first version and a rough range. Does that work?

q.q: Things they could not answer or need to check
q.client: Anything you still need to find out or decide?

q.q: What I promised to send, and by when
q.client: Anything you would like us to send you?

q.q: Next call or follow-up date
q.client: When is a good time for a follow-up call?

parts.title: Private notes
parts.say: Not shown to the person interviewed. Fill in right after the call while it is fresh.

q.q: Your read: clarity, energy, who talked, what they care about most
Signals to weigh
o: No budget, or would not discuss it
Wants equity or revenue share instead of payment
Marketplace with two sides to fill
Needs money to move through the app

q.q: Gut viability
Questions for the scoping session
